evidence.record_quote: Labor Notes is best known for our monthly magazine of the same name.
Labor news from labor's point of view. $30 for 11 issues.
Every two years Labor Notes holds a national conference that attracts thousands of activists, about a tenth of them from other countries.
Labor Notes works with local unions and community groups to organize Troublemakers Schools

atoms.reference: To promote organizing, aggressive strategies and union democracy through a rank-and-file network.

evidence.record_quote: Through our magazine, website, books, conferences, and workshops, we promote organizing, aggressive strategies to take on employers, labor-community solidarity, and unions that are run by their members.
Labor Notes is also a network of rank-and-file members, local union leaders, and labor activists who know the labor movement is worth fighting for.

atoms.reference: An independent publication, free to print the voices who say the movement could be doing better.

evidence.record_quote: And as an independent publication, we’re free to include the voices who say we could be doing better—and tell how.
For the most part, our leaders are doing a poor job of navigating us through the crisis.

atoms.span: Labor Notes is an American media and organizing project
founded in 1979 by labor activist Kim Moody
it reports on rank-and-file union democracy, strikes, and independent worker-led organizing efforts.
Publishes 11 issues annually covering shop-floor strategy, union elections, and grassroots campaigns across major sectors.
Operating as a voice for the "troublemaking wing" of the labor movement
